project_scope.note: Current canonical website anchor is Turk's cap; broader family exceptions remain a later visual expansion.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Go to the flower center: local mallows commonly have numerous stamens fused into a conspicuous staminal column around the style. Then confirm stipules, palmate venation/stellate hairs and the fruit.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Commonly alternate/spiral and stipulate; palmate venation and stellate hairs are frequent supporting characters.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Local Malvoideae commonly has 5 petals and many stamens fused into a tube/column; epicalyx may be present or absent.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Can be dry segmented mericarps or fleshy segmented fruit in local examples.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Use the staminal column as a strong local mallow cue, but not as an absolute definition of broad Malvaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → diagnostic structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Turk's cap is a terrific staminal-column teacher because the petals stay furled and the reproductive column sticks out in plain view.

steps.title: 1 · Find the projecting column
steps.look_for: A long central column carrying many anthers around the style.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the fastest local Malvoideae recognition feature.

steps.title: 2 · Notice the furled petals
steps.look_for: Five red petals remain rolled/furled instead of opening flat.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows that a mallow need not look like a flat Hibiscus flower.

steps.title: 3 · Check the leaf surface
steps.look_for: Cordate/lobed leaf with palmate veins and stellate pubescence.

steps.title: 4 · Follow to fleshy fruit
steps.look_for: A fleshy red segmented fruit rather than a dry Callirhoe-style schizocarp.

comparisons.title: Malvaceae vs Papaveraceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have many stamens. Local mallows commonly fuse them into a staminal column; prickly poppies have numerous free stamens and a capsule.

visual_lesson.caveat: Broad Malvaceae is more diverse than the classic Hibiscus/Turk's-cap flower plan.

family_confusion_cleanup.look_here_first: In local Malvoideae inspect the central staminal column with many anthers around the style; then calyx/epicalyx, stipules, and mature fruit. The column is not universal across broad Malvaceae.

comparisons.difference: Usually free stamens rather than a fused staminal column; compare flower centers and capsule versus mallow mericarps.
Argemone has free stamens and a syncarpous capsule; many local mallows have a staminal column and segmented fruit.
Geranium and Erodium have free stamens and conspicuously beaked schizocarps.
Stellate hairs alone do not decide family; compare unisexual flowers and often three-part capsules against mallow floral column and mericarps.

exceptions: Epicalyx variable; Callirhoe leiocarpa is an important no-epicalyx comparison.
Malvaviscus has fleshy fruit unlike dry mericarps of Callirhoe, Abutilon and Sida.
Fused staminal column is a local Malvoideae cue, not universal Malvaceae.
genus_routing: Malvaviscus: furled petals, exserted staminal column, fleshy fruit.
Callirhoe: check epicalyx and dry mericarps.
Abutilon: count style branches and inspect mericarp tips; use existing genus comparison.
Sida: small flowers, dry mericarps and calyx.
Sphaeralcea: stellate foliage and mallow flower; use fruit rather than color.
